newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean banks' operating profits rise 16.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean banks' operating profits rise 16.2 pct.

text.p: Combined operating profits of South Korea's 25 commercial banks -- 15 nationwide banks and 10 regional banks -- rose 16.2 pct to 4.17 trillion won in 1996 from 3.59 trillion in 1995, the Bank of Korea said on Thursday.

"Interest income, which rose 25.2 percent to 7.31 trillion won, contributed mainly to the rise in operating profits," said Lee Suk-keun, deputy drector at the central bank's supervisory planning division.
But net profits in the period fell 2.4 percent to 846.8 billion won from 867.6 billion due to losses from investment in securities, it said in a statement.
The central bank said the book value of the banks' securities holdings fell by an estimated 895.2 billion won. The value fell by 543.7 billion in 1995.
Lee said a slump in the Seoul bourse was to blame for the rise. The composite stock index closed 1996 at a year low of 651.22, sharply lower from 882.94 at the start of the year.
Non-interest income fell 13.6 percent to 1.77 trillion won in 1996 from 2.05 trillion in 1995, the bank said.
The Kookmim Bank topped the list of operating profits with 503 billion won, up 41.3 percent from a year earlier.
